statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib vulnerability in the Docker base image. Liquibase is a Java application and does not execute Go code at runtime. The Go binary is part of Docker base image tooling and is not invoked by Liquibase.

statements.status_notes: Due to the design of the name constraint checking algorithm, the processing time of some inputs scale non-linearly with respect to the size of the certificate. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 name-constraint vulnerability. NVD fixes the 1.25 line in Go 1.25.3 and the 1.24 line in Go 1.24.9; the scanner reported go1.25.1 for this image. Liquibase Secure only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:39-55), and the entrypoint only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Repo-wide source greps found no crypto/x509, SystemCertPool, or CertPool usage in application code, so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which contain DSA public keys can cause programs to panic, due to a interface cast that assumes they implement the Equal method. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Validating certificate chains with DSA public keys is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no custom RootCAs or PEM loading logic (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

statements.status_notes: The processing time for parsing some invalid inputs scales non-linearly with respect to the size of the input. This affects programs which parse untrusted PEM inputs.
statements.impact_statement: Untrusted PEM parsing is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no PEM parsing or certificate-loader code (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the invalid-PEM parsing path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

statements.status_notes: The Reader.ReadResponse function constructs a response string through repeated string concatenation of lines. When the number of lines in a response is large, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Reader.ReadResponse CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ReadResponse, net/textproto, or net/http usage, so the vulnerable API is not directly reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: The ParseAddress function constructs domain-literal address components through repeated string concatenation. When parsing large domain-literal components, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib ParseAddress CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ParseAddress or net/mail usage, so the vulnerable email parsing API is not reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: Building a malicious file with cmd/go can cause can cause a write to an attacker-controlled file with partial control of the file content. The "#cgo pkg-config:" directive in a Go source file provides command-line arguments to provide to the Go pkg-config command. An attacker can provide a "--log-file" argument to this directive, causing pkg-config to write to an attacker-controlled location.

Repo-wide grep found no runtime `go build`, `go mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN`, `GOMODPROXY`, `GOSUMDB`, `pkg-config`, or `cgo` usage, so the vulnerable cmd/go path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 VerifyHostname quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib versions in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images. The Secure Dockerfile installs lpm as an optional helper (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49), but the Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); otherwise it executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119). A focused grep across the Docker runtime files found no direct VerifyHostname, Certificate.Verify, matchHostnames, HostnameError, or crypto/x509 usage. Defense in depth: current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Go stdlib crypto/x509 DoS vulnerability (GO-2026-4947). Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 certificate policy mapping DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Go stdlib internal/syscall/unix Root.Chmod symlink traversal vulnerability. Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/tls TLS 1.3 key update DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

statements.status_notes: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

statements.status_notes: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib recursion-limit issue in Unmarshal. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). The default Liquibase runtime path executes the Java CLI directly, so the Unmarshal path that would process attacker-controlled deeply nested data is not exercised. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-5972 alias.

statements.status_notes: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail CPU exhaustion via pathological inputs to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail parsing functions are not called by lpm at any point during package installation or management operations.

CVE-2026-39821 / GO-2026-5026 is the Go idna / net/http hostname validation issue, but the lpm helper only downloads from code-defined hosts. `cmd/populator/modules.go:20` and `cmd/populator/modules.go:25` hardcode the module registry URL, `cmd/populator/Populator.go:23` and `cmd/populator/Populator.go:29` show only the embedded package manifest is iterated, and the HTTP helpers consume those fixed URLs (`cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:28`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:30`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:31`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:32`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:13`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:25`). There is no attacker-controlled hostname input path here, so the Punycode hostname-validation bug is unreachable in this deployment.

statements.status_notes: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, root.Open("symlink/") will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib os.Root symlink-following vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.12, 1.26.5, and 1.27.0-rc.2. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib version v1.26.4 in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49) — confirmed by extracting the released liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 binary and running `go version` on it, which reports go1.26.4, matching the scanner's reported installed version exactly. The vulnerable API, os.Root (and OpenRoot), is a defensive filesystem-sandboxing API added in Go 1.24; a source-level grep of the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 repository for os.Root, OpenRoot, and .Root( returned zero hits, so lpm does not use the vulnerable API at all. Defense in depth: the Secure Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); the default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly and never calls lpm (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119-121).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib html/template escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no html/template usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/http/httputil ReverseProxy query sanitization vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no ReverseProxy or net/http/httputil usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.

The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation. This vulnerability affects any user using an untrusted module proxy (GOMODPROXY) or checksum database (GOSUMDB). A malicious module proxy can serve altered versions of the Go toolchain. When selecting a different version of the Go toolchain than the currently installed toolchain (due to the GOTOOLCHAIN environment variable, or a go.work or go.mod with a toolchain line), the go command will download and execute a toolchain provided by the module proxy. A malicious module proxy can bypass checksum database validation for this downloaded toolchain.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib toolchain-download checksum validation flaw fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. The Secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the only runtime invocation is `lpm add mysql --global` behind INSTALL_MYSQL (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4 and docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). Repo-wide grep found no runtime `go build`, `go mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN`, `GOMODPROXY`, `GOSUMDB`, `pkg-config`, or `cgo` usage, so the vulnerable toolchain-download path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation.
statements.impact_statement: Go checksum-validation flaw in cmd/go only applies when the Go toolchain downloads modules or toolchains from an untrusted proxy or checksum database. Liquibase Secure installs lpm from a release ZIP (`docker/Dockerfile:39`) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4`). This image does not execute `go`, use GOTOOLCHAIN, or perform module downloads at runtime.

statements.status_notes: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib mime.WordDecoder.DecodeHeader quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35) from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49). The Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). A reachability grep across docker and core found no WordDecoder.DecodeHeader, mime.WordDecoder, encoded-word, MIME header, net/mail, ReadMIMEHeader, or textproto usage, so the vulnerable MIME header decoding path is not reachable from the Liquibase Secure Docker runtime.

CVE-2026-46600 / GO-2026-5942 requires the Go cgo DNS resolver and invalid SVCB/HTTPS DNS answers, but the lpm release build disables cgo (`Makefile:21`, `Makefile:22`, `Makefile:36`, and `Makefile:37` set `CGO_ENABLED=0`). The runtime code only creates ordinary HTTP clients and performs fixed-URL downloads (`internal/app/utils/Http.go:13`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:25`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:28`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:30`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:31`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:32`), so the cgo resolver path used by the advisory is not reachable here.

statements.status_notes: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 preface timeout issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure is a database migration CLI, not an HTTP server. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5), so the server-side unencrypted HTTP/2 listener required by the advisory is absent.

statements.status_notes: Previously, pathological inputs could close an unescaped '/' early, allowing for attack-controlled data to inject arbitrary content, potentially leading to XSS.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib unescaped-slash parsing issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure's runtime path is the Java CLI plus the optional lpm helper (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50 and core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). The container does not parse attacker-controlled HTML/XML content through this stdlib path, so the vulnerable behavior is not exercised.

statements.status_notes: Previously, DecodeElement would reset the depth counter causing it to never fire; this could lead to stack exhaustion.

Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5), so the XML decode path that would process attacker-controlled nested elements is not reached. statements.status_notes: Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead.

The secure Docker image only executes the Java CLI by default and invokes lpm 0.3.6 only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50 and core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). The vulnerable path resolution behavior is not exercised on attacker-controlled input in this deployment.

statements.status_notes: Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib KeyUpdate state-advance issue in TLS handshakes. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The server-side TLS handshake path required by the advisory is absent.

crypto/x509 name-constraint quadratic behavior is not reachable in the Liquibase Secure container. A repo-wide search found no code path that parses attacker-controlled certificate chains or invokes the affected x509 name-constraint APIs at runtime.

encoding/pem quadratic parsing behavior is not reachable in the Liquibase Secure container. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh: 4). A repo-wide search found no code path that parses untrusted PEM input at runtime.

Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the upstream liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 go.mod declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which is newer than the scanner-reported Go 1.25.1 and includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase/liquibase-package-manager found no crypto/x509 imports or references, so the vulnerable certificate-chain path is not exercised by lpm source.
